content:
Marissa Cole: PRD question we need to settle today: for GA, are guardrails *only* visual + notifications (soft-stop), or do we actually auto-stop traffic (hard-stop)?

Paula Mendes: +1. The PRD currently says “automatic rollback triggers” but we’ve been talking about “soft-stop + banner + paging” in eng sync.

Dylan Brooks: engineering preference is soft-stop for initial GA. we can do hard-stop later once we’re confident in data quality + false positive rate.

Sean Gallagher: from SRE side, I’m nervous about hard-stop being the default. if our attribution drops or propagation lags, you’ll page and then auto-stop the wrong thing.

Jada Williams: also, hard-stop semantics are messy w/ rollout policies. if a route is in canary AND experiment, what is “rollback” even doing? (stop experiment? revert policy? both?)

Chloe Martin: + we don’t have the full state machine for “stopping” nailed yet (immediate vs drain). soft-stop just marks as degraded + blocks ramps.

Marissa Cole: ok but customers are going to assume guardrails “protect” them. what’s the honest promise?

Rafael Mendes: we can promise: guardrails evaluate continuously and will (1) alert, (2) mark experiment Degraded, (3) recommend stop, (4) provide one-click stop. Optional auto-stop only for severe thresholds + with kill switch.

Allison Grant: please don’t call it “automatic rollback” in GA if it’s not deterministic + safe. call it “guardrail alerts + stop automation (optional)” or similar.

Paula Mendes: what does “soft-stop” mean in UI terms? banner? disable ramp? stop button becomes primary?

Dylan Brooks: what we’ve prototyped: status changes to “Degraded” and top banner says which guardrail breached (p99 latency, error, cost/token, quality). It also links to dashboard + audit trail.

Logan Wright: re: false positives — telemetry gaps are real, esp streaming + retries. we’re still fixing attribution. hard-stop based on partial data is dangerous.

Selene Huang: quality signals are also sampled. if traffic split is small, quality metric variance is high. hard-stop on quality regression is definitely not GA-ready.

Marissa Cole: makes sense. so maybe: latency/error guardrails can be “hard-stop eligible” but off by default?

Sean Gallagher: if we do any hard-stop in GA, I want:
- default OFF
- explicit opt-in per experiment
- documented thresholds + minimum sample size/time window
- global kill switch + oncall playbook

Rafael Mendes: +1 and add “cooldown” / “two-window confirm” so we don’t flap.

Chloe Martin: implementation note: we can support an `auto_stop_policy` field in config but ignore unless enabled. Then GA UI can surface it as “beta” toggle.

Paula Mendes: PRD wording proposal:
- GA: Guardrails with notifications + Console banners; recommended stop; one-click stop.
- GA+: Optional automatic stop for severe regressions (latency/error) behind feature flag; not for quality.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: and we’ll keep “hard-stop” as a follow-up milestone.

Marissa Cole: are we aligned that “soft-stop” does NOT change traffic routing automatically?

Jada Williams: correct. soft-stop = we continue routing per the experiment allocation, but we set experiment state to Degraded and block further ramp actions. (and we can optionally auto-set allocation back to 0 if hard-stop is enabled).

Allison Grant: also important: audit log entries should show *who* hit stop, and if an auto-stop triggered, we need actor = system + reason.

Logan Wright: if we do hard-stop later, pls make sure it’s robust to propagation lag. otherwise we’ll “stop” in control plane but routers keep serving old config for N minutes.

Sean Gallagher: yup. if config staleness > threshold we should disable auto-stop entirely (or at least require confirmation).

Connor O'Brien: release note implications: if GA messaging changes, I need final copy by EOW for the beta→GA comms. also we should not commit to “automatic rollback” publicly.

Paula Mendes: ok, what do we call it in Console? “Auto-stop” vs “Auto-rollback”?

Dylan Brooks: “Auto-stop” is less overloaded. “Rollback” suggests revert to previous model version etc.

Marissa Cole: agreed. we’ll use “Auto-stop” for experiments.

Selene Huang: and in the UI copy: “Auto-stop will stop the experiment and send all traffic to the Control variant.” (assuming control is defined)

Jada Williams: edge case: experiments without clear “control” (A/B/n). we should require a designated control variant if auto-stop is enabled.

Chloe Martin: +1. can enforce in validation: `auto_stop_enabled` => `control_variant_id` required.

Rafael Mendes: thresholds for GA defaults (soft-stop only):
- p99 latency regression > 20% vs control for 10m
- error rate > 1% absolute OR > 2x control for 10m
- cost/token > 15% vs control for 30m
Quality = alert only, no stop.

Sean Gallagher: those seem reasonable but keep them as defaults only. customers have different SLOs.

Marissa Cole: action items:
1) I’ll update PRD language: guardrails = alerts + degraded state; no default auto-stop in GA.
2) Dylan/Chloe: add note to eng plan: config supports `auto_stop` but gated + not surfaced as GA promise.
3) Sean/Rafael: define minimum requirements for enabling auto-stop (kill switch, runbook, thresholds).

Dylan Brooks: sounds good. I’ll also add a PRD comment: “soft-stop” terminology is internal; customer-facing is “Degraded + alert.”

Paula Mendes: I’ll sync w/ design to make sure the results view isn’t implying traffic was changed automatically.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: pls tag me on the PRD update so I can align launch checklist + comms.

Allison Grant: one more: dashboards should label “guardrail breached” vs “auto-stop triggered” distinctly. don’t want confusion.

Marissa Cole: yep. will incorporate. thanks all.
